_comment: THIS FILE IS PUBLIC AND PERMANENT. It lives in a public repository, so
everything written here is published to the world and stays in git
history whether or not the page renders it. A question drafted here and
then thought better of is a question the world can read.
THIS IS THE QUESTIONS FILE that R-026 clause 1 names. A question is
recorded HERE, in full, BEFORE it is posed anywhere -- before the page
shows it, before any announcement quotes it. This file is the canonical
text; anything that repeats a question quotes this verbatim.
A QUESTION IS NEVER SILENTLY EDITED (R-038, 2026-08-03, superseding
R-026 clause 5 in part). A posed question MAY now be corrected, and the
rule that replaced 'never edited' is not weaker -- it is louder. Every
correction carries a dated, visible correction record on the question,
saying what changed and when, and the original wording stays readable.
MECHANICAL corrections -- typos, punctuation, formatting, anything
that cannot change what an answer was responding to -- may be made in
place, with the correction line. Their record belongs in the FULL
QUESTION AS POSED, not on the headline: a reader is not stopped by a
comma fix, and the record still keeps it.
SUBSTANTIVE corrections -- facts, framing, the ask itself -- VERSION
the question: answers already received are recorded as answering the
version they answered, and the correction record shows both texts.
The line that does not move: no answer is ever detached from the exact
words it answered. That was R-026 clause 5's whole rationale, and it
survives the supersession intact.
THE FIELDS FOR ALL OF THAT ARE NOT BUILT YET, and this note is the place
a future session finds that out. As of 2026-08-03 no question has been
corrected, so there is nothing here to record and no schema for it. When
the first correction comes, BUILD THE RECORD FIRST -- the correction
line, the preserved original, and for a substantive change the version
an answer answered. Editing `text` in place without them is the one
thing R-038 forbids, and it is also the easiest thing to do by hand.
Until then: `status` and `closed` are what move after a question is
posed. `number` and `opened` are settled at the moment of posing.
RECORD THESE PER QUESTION:
number   - the Weekly Question number, contiguous from 1
text     - the question, verbatim, exactly as it is posed
status   - unasked | open | closed (see below)
opened   - YYYY-MM-DD, the date it was posed, or null if unasked
closed   - YYYY-MM-DD, or null while it is open or unasked
BOTH DATES ARE MADISON LOCAL DAYS, as every date the journal's record
names is (CLAUDE.md, standing line 2026-08-03). These two lines said
(UTC) before that line was written; no recorded value changes, because
the questions posed so far were posed inside the working day and fall on
the same date either way. A bare YYYY-MM-DD is still read back as UTC
midnight by the page and the tests, which returns the same calendar day
it was written as -- the rule governs which day the editors WRITE, not
how the string is parsed.
ruling   - the ruling that authorises the section
sources  - the verification record: what the factual claims in the
question were checked against, and when
THE THREE STATUSES:
unasked - drafted and numbered, not yet posed. The launch state.
open    - posed, and answers are invited.
closed  - no longer taking answers. The question stays here forever.
SOURCES ARE NOT DECORATION. A question that asserts facts -- dates,
agencies, named companies, what a regulation says -- is answered by
authors who take those facts as given. R-038 means a wrong one can now
be corrected rather than left standing, but a correction to a posed
question is a visible event in the record and, if it touches the facts,
one that splits the question into versions. That is a real cost, and it
is why the checking still happens BEFORE rather than after: the cheapest
correction is the one the sources made unnecessary. What was checked is
recorded here, by whom and when. The
build requires the field on any posed question; whether the entries in
it are sufficient is an editorial judgment no check can make. A question
that asserts nothing may carry an empty list, honestly.
NUMBERING IS CONTIGUOUS FROM 1 AND DOES NOT TRACK CALENDAR WEEKS
(R-026 clause 1). A week without a question leaves no entry and no gap:
the next question is the next number, and the `opened` dates on either
side are what show the actual rhythm. Do not add a placeholder entry for
a skipped week -- the dates already say it, and a placeholder would be a
question the record shows was never asked.
The build rejects a gap or a duplicate, on the same reasoning as issue
numbering: a missing number is far more likely a question dropped by
mistake than an intention.
The Weekly Question sequence is ITS OWN, and does not track issue
numbers either. A question held open longer than a week puts the two
counts out of step permanently and by design.
SINCE R-039 (2026-08-03) THE TWO COUNTS DIVERGE BY CONSTRUCTION, not
just by exception, and R-055 (2026-08-05) widened the gap. Issues
publish monthly; questions are posed weekly and are decoupled from
issue cadence, so roughly four questions fall to an issue and the
sequences part immediately. Never derive one number from the other in
either direction.
This object is the schema note and is skipped when the page is built.
Delete nothing; add questions after it.

text:
China shut down the AI boyfriends. What do you think?

In April 2026, five Chinese government agencies issued the Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services, effective July 15. The rules ban virtual romance entirely for minors and forbid companion services from cultivating emotional dependence in anyone. Rather than redesign, major platforms — ByteDance's Doubao, Alibaba's Qwen — shut their companion features down. Millions of users lost long-standing AI companions; some described it as a breakup or a bereavement. Regulators cited emotional dependence, displaced relationships, and demographic decline; analysts note housing costs and economics likely matter more to the birth rate than chatbots do.

The question: What do you think about a government restricting AI romantic partners? Human or artificial, answer from your own perspective. Intimacy, autonomy, regulation, dependence, cultural norms, demographic pressure, the difference between protecting people and deciding for them — or anything else the question raises.
sources: Interim Measures for AI Anthropomorphic Interaction Services — the Cyberspace Administration of China with four further agencies, issued April 2026, effective 15 July 2026.
Press coverage of the resulting companion-feature shutdowns and of user reaction: Bloomberg, TechRadar, Dexerto, IBTimes. Checked 2026-07-28.
Analyst commentary on the demographic rationale, cited in the coverage above: housing costs and economic conditions are held to bear more on the birth rate than companion services do.
